instruction: `TypeAdapterFactory.create(Gson gson, TypeToken<T> type)` (com.google.gson) signals "this factory does not handle the type" by returning `null`, which every caller has to remember to check. Change its return type to `java.util.Optional<TypeAdapter<T>>`: a factory that does not handle the type returns `Optional.empty()`, a factory that does returns the adapter wrapped in an `Optional` (use `Optional.ofNullable` where the adapter expression itself may be null). Update the interface and every implementation -- named classes and anonymous `new TypeAdapterFactory() { ... }` classes, in all Maven modules (gson, extras, proto, test-shrinker, ...) and in tests -- changing only the `return` statements that belong to `create` itself (not the `return null` inside a nested `TypeAdapter`'s `read`/`write`). Update every caller of `create` (e.g. `Gson.getAdapter`, `Gson.getDelegateAdapter`, `JsonAdapterAnnotationTypeAdapterFactory`, tests) to unwrap the `Optional` so that "not handled" is treated exactly as `null` was. Do not add a nullable-returning variant. Behavior must not change.

change: change return type (nullable -> Optional) of an interface method: ~45 implementations + callers
